# How AI Works for Kids

> Free, hands-on lessons that show kids ages 6–10 how AI works. Kids teach a tiny AI named Pip, then test it and fix its mistakes. No ads, no accounts, no live chatbot. Built by Nick Castro in Chicago.

Every game runs a small model inside the web page (a nearest-neighbor sorter, a decision stump, and a word-counting next-word model). Nothing a child does is sent to an AI service. Progress is stored in the browser only.

## Lessons

1. [Meet Pip: What is AI?](https://howaiworksforkids.com/lessons/what-is-ai): AI learns patterns from examples, then guesses. Game: AI Detective
2. [Teach by Showing](https://howaiworksforkids.com/lessons/learning-from-examples): Learning from examples. Game: Sort the Glorbs (a real nearest-neighbor model)
3. [How Chatbots Talk](https://howaiworksforkids.com/lessons/guess-the-next-word): Chatbots guess the next word. Game: Next Word! and Story Builder
4. [Good Examples In, Good Guesses Out](https://howaiworksforkids.com/lessons/sneaky-clues): Lopsided data teaches the wrong clue. Game: Fix Pip's Mix-up
5. [Sure Doesn't Mean Right](https://howaiworksforkids.com/lessons/ai-can-be-wrong): AI can sound sure and be wrong. Game: Fact or Fib?
6. [Real or Made by AI?](https://howaiworksforkids.com/lessons/real-or-made-up): AI-made pictures and videos. Game: Spot the Glitches
7. [Be the Boss of AI](https://howaiworksforkids.com/lessons/smart-and-safe): Privacy, AI isn't a person, ask a grown-up. Game: Go, Ask, or Stop
